source.title: Matthew Henry's Concise Commentary on the Whole Bible
source.author: Matthew Henry

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: A right cause will be better pleaded with meekness than with passion. Nothing stirs up anger like grievous words.

entries.heading: Verse 2
entries.text: He that has knowledge, is to use it aright, for the good of others.

entries.heading: Verse 3
entries.text: Secret sins, services, and sorrows, are under God's eye. This speaks comfort to saints, and terror to sinners.

entries.heading: Verse 4
entries.text: A good tongue is healing to wounded consciences, by comforting them; to sin-sick souls, by convincing them; and it reconciles parties at variance.

entries.heading: Verse 5
entries.text: If instruction is despised, reprove men rather than suffer them to go on undisturbed in the way to ruin.

entries.heading: Verse 6
entries.text: The wealth of worldly men increases their fears and suspicions, adds strength to their passions, and renders the fear of death more distressing.

entries.heading: Verse 7
entries.text: We use knowledge aright when we disperse it; but the heart of the foolish has nothing to disperse that is good.

entries.heading: Verses 8-9
entries.text: The wicked put other things in the stead of Christ's atonement, or in the place of holy obedience. Praying graces are his gift, and the work of his Spirit, with which he is well pleased.

entries.heading: Verse 10
entries.text: He that hates reproof shall perish in his sins, since he would not be parted from them.

entries.heading: Verse 11
entries.text: There is nothing that can be hid from the eyes of God, not even man's thoughts.

entries.heading: Verse 12
entries.text: A scorner cannot bear to reflect seriously within his own heart.

entries.heading: Verse 13
entries.text: A gloomy, impatient, unthankful spirit, springing from pride and undue attachment to worldly objects, renders a man uneasy to himself and others.

entries.heading: Verse 14
entries.text: A wise man seeks to gain more wisdom, growing in grace and in the knowledge of Christ. But a carnal mind rests contented, flattering itself.

entries.heading: Verse 15
entries.text: Some are much in affliction, and of a sorrowful spirit. Such are to be pitied, prayed for, and comforted. And others serve God with gladness of heart, and it prompts their obedience, yet they should rejoice with trembling.

entries.heading: Verses 16-17
entries.text: Believers often have enough when worldly eyes see little; the Lord is with them, without the cares, troubles, and temptations which are with the wealth of the wicked.

entries.heading: Verse 18
entries.text: He that is slow to anger, not only prevents strife, but appeases it, if kindled.

entries.heading: Verse 19
entries.text: Those who have no heart to their work, pretend that they cannot do their work without hardship and danger. And thus many live always in doubt about their state, because always in neglect of some duty.

entries.heading: Verse 20
entries.text: Those who treat an aged mother or a father with contempt or neglect, show their own folly.

entries.heading: Verse 21
entries.text: Such as are truly wise, study that their thoughts, words, and actions should be regular, sincere, and holy.

entries.heading: Verse 22
entries.text: If men will not take time and pains to deliberate, they are not likely to bring any thing to pass.

entries.heading: Verse 23
entries.text: Wisdom is needed to suit our discourse to the occasions.

entries.heading: Verse 24
entries.text: A good man sets his affections on things above; his way leads directly thither.

entries.heading: Verse 25
entries.text: Pride is the ruin of multitudes. But those who are in affliction God will support.

entries.heading: Verse 26
entries.text: The thoughts of wicked men offend Him who knows the heart.

entries.heading: Verse 27
entries.text: The covetous man lets none of his family have rest or enjoyment. And greediness of gain often tempts to projects that bring ruin.

entries.heading: Verse 28
entries.text: A good man is proved to be a wise man by this; he governs his tongue well.

entries.heading: Verse 29
entries.text: God sets himself at a distance from those who set him at defiance.

entries.heading: Verse 30
entries.text: How delightful to the humbled soul to hear the good report of salvation by the Lord Jesus Christ!

entries.heading: Verse 31
entries.text: Faithful, friendly reproofs help spiritual life, and lead to eternal life.

entries.heading: Verse 32
entries.text: Sinners undervalue their own souls; therefore they prefer the body before the soul, and wrong the soul to please the body.

entries.heading: Verse 33
entries.text: The fear of the Lord will dispose us to search the Scriptures with reverence; and it will cause us to follow the leadings of the Holy Spirit. While we humbly place all our dependence on the grace of God, we are exalted in the righteousness of Christ.
